item.title: About
item.description:
I’m Chris Coletta, a data scientist based in Baltimore, Maryland. I work across data architecture, engineering, and analysis, with a particular interest in how complex measurements become reliable evidence.

From physical models to data systems

I began in mechanical engineering at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where my research involved finite-element modeling of muscle forces on skeletal structures. Commercial software development at Vistagy then gave me experience building tools for aerospace manufacturing.

item.title: Baltimore Quantitative
item.description:
Baltimore Quantitative is my independent consulting business, based in Baltimore, Maryland. I help research teams make complex data consistent, documented, and ready for analysis.

Bring the data together

Scientific datasets often arrive from different partners, instruments, and collection periods. I help reconcile variable definitions, units, repeated measurements, and delivery formats so the resulting dataset preserves its meaning.

Make quality visible

Quality checks should answer practical questions: what changed, what is inconsistent, and what needs investigation? I build repeatable validation and reconciliation processes that make those questions easier to answer.

item.title: Experience
item.description:
My experience spans the full path from raw measurements to usable data: understanding sources, designing models, building pipelines, validating results, and helping teams maintain what they build.

Fearless

Consultant, Data & Analytics · September 2022–present · Baltimore

At Fearless, I work on public-sector data architecture and engineering. My assignments have included:

  • Maryland FAMLI — platform architecture: compared Databricks and AWS-native lakehouse approaches and developed implementation blueprints, engineering standards, and governance practices.
  • OPM/USPS Postal Service Health Benefits — data pipelines: architected enrollment and eligibility processing in Databricks, with reconciliation, exception handling, and monitoring.
  • SEC Data Prism — structured data integration: built XML-to-relational transformations, automated schema generation, and AWS Glue and Airflow workflows using Apache Iceberg.
  • CDC — distributed analytics: migrated disease-surveillance processing from local R workflows to Databricks using SparkR and sparklyr, and contributed governance guidance.
  • USDA Farm Loan Program — legacy modernization: reconstructed COBOL/IDMS mainframe data models and prepared schema documentation and migration artifacts.
  • USGS 3DEP — geospatial discovery: built a prototype for publishing and discovering geospatial data using containerized services and STAC metadata.
  • Team development: mentoring engineers through pair programming, technical reviews, and coaching.

This work is performed through my role at Fearless. Read the OPM career spotlight →
